conceptName: Customizing the engine with pluggable operations

items.stem: How does the engine discover a custom operation class like a preprocessor or duplication rule?

options.text: You implement the operation's interface, annotate the class with its attribute, and MEF discovers it — the same pattern as feeds and sinks
You register it by hand in a central list in Program.cs
You modify the Synnduit engine source to call it
You add it to a Segment in appsettings.json

items.explanation: Operation classes follow the same interface + attribute + MEF-discovery pattern as feeds and sinks; dependencies come in via [ImportingConstructor].

misconceptions.b: MEF discovers parts by their attributes — there's no central registration list.
misconceptions.c: The whole point is extending the engine without modifying it (L1.3).

items.stem: You must decide whether a source record is 'already in the destination' by calling a SharePoint API (a stored key can't express it). Which extension point fits?

options.text: A [DuplicationRule] / IDuplicationRule<T> — its GetDuplicates() runs your own match logic and returns Duplicates with a MatchWeight
A [DuplicationKey] attribute on a POCO property

items.explanation: A custom duplication rule replaces the default key-based matching with your own logic — here, an API lookup — returning matches with a MatchWeight.

misconceptions.b: [DuplicationKey] matches on a stored property value; it can't perform an API lookup.
misconceptions.c: A preprocessor transforms/rejects entities; it doesn't perform duplicate matching.

items.stem: Inside a [PreprocessorOperation], you call preprocessorEntity.Reject() when a value can't be resolved. What outcome does that produce?

options.text: Rejected — a clean deferral (the record isn't ready this run), not a failure
ExceptionThrown — it's treated as an error
NewEntityCreated — the record is inserted anyway

items.explanation: Reject() defers the record, producing the Rejected outcome (L1.10) — explicitly not an error; it can be retried on a later run.

misconceptions.b: Reject() is a deliberate deferral, distinct from ExceptionThrown.
misconceptions.d: Rejecting one record doesn't abort the run.

items.stem: Which of these is NOT one of the engine's pluggable operation extension points?

options.text: [EntityType] — it identifies a POCO's type, it isn't an operation class

items.explanation: [PreprocessorOperation], [Homogenizer], and [EventReceiver] mark discovered operation classes. [EntityType] is part of the POCO contract (L1.9), not an operation you implement.

misconceptions.c: [Homogenizer] is a real operation type — it normalizes a value before comparison.
misconceptions.d: [EventReceiver] is a real operation type — it receives engine events.

items.stem: A source feed delivers calendar events whose category is a set of source-system GUIDs, but the destination needs the mapped destination category IDs — and an event whose category can't be resolved should not sync yet. Which extension point do you use, and sketch how it behaves?
rubric: Use a [PreprocessorOperation] implementing IPreprocessorOperation<T> (transform-before-sync hook), discovered by MEF like a feed/sink
In Preprocess(), for source-origin entities, resolve each source category GUID to its destination category ID (e.g. via IMapper) and set the destination field
If a category can't be resolved, log and call Reject() — producing the Rejected outcome (L1.10), a deferral that retries on a later run rather than an error
items.sampleAnswer: Write a [PreprocessorOperation] class implementing IPreprocessorOperation<TeamSiteCalendarEvent>; MEF discovers it like any feed/sink. In Preprocess(), for source-origin entities I map each source-system category GUID to its destination category ID (via the injected IMapper) and set the destination CategoryIds field. If any category can't be resolved, I log an error and call entity.Reject(), which produces the Rejected outcome (L1.10) — the event is deferred and retried on a later run once its category exists, rather than failing. The context, mapper, and logger are injected via [ImportingConstructor].
